segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: After Jesus had said these things, he lifted his eyes to heaven and said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Father, the hour has come. Glorify your Son, so that the Son may glorify you,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: just as you gave him authority over all flesh, so that he might give eternal life to all whom you have given him.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And this is eternal life: that they may know you, the only true God, and the one you sent, Jesus Christ.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I glorified you on the earth by completing the work you have given me to do.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And now, Father, glorify me in your own presence with the glory I had in your presence before the world existed.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I revealed your name to the people you gave me out of the world. They were yours, and you gave them to me, and they have kept your word.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Now they have come to know that everything you have given me is from you,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: because the words you gave me I have given to them, and they received them and came to know in truth that I came from you, and they believed that you sent me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I am asking on their behalf. I am not asking on behalf of the world but on behalf of those you have given me, because they are yours,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and all that is mine is yours, and what is yours is mine, and I have been glorified in them.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I am no longer in the world, but they are in the world, and I am coming to you. Holy Father, keep them in your name, which you have given me, so that they may be one just as we are.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: While I was with them, I kept them in your name, which you have given me. I guarded them, and not one of them was lost except the son of destruction, so that the scripture might be fulfilled.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But now I am coming to you, and I am saying these things in the world so that they may have my joy made full in themselves.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I have given them your word, and the world has hated them, because they are not of the world, just as I am not of the world.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I am not asking that you take them out of the world, but that you keep them from the evil one.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: They are not of the world, just as I am not of the world.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Consecrate them in the truth; your word is truth.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Just as you sent me into the world, I also have sent them into the world.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And for their sake I consecrate myself, so that they too may be consecrated in truth.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I am not asking on behalf of these only, but also on behalf of those who believe in me through their word,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: that they may all be one, just as you, Father, are in me and I in you, that they too may be in us, so that the world may believe that you sent me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: The glory you have given me I have given to them, so that they may be one just as we are one,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I in them and you in me, so that they may be made completely one, so that the world may know that you sent me and loved them just as you loved me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Father, I want those you have given me to be with me where I am, so that they may see my glory, which you have given me because you loved me before the foundation of the world.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Righteous Father, the world has not known you, but I have known you, and these have come to know that you sent me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I made your name known to them, and I will make it known, so that the love with which you loved me may be in them, and I in them.”

notes.note: A Semitic expression, familiar from the Greek Old Testament, for all humanity, often with a hint of human frailty before God. Many modern translations paraphrase it as 'all people'. The literal phrase is kept here because the Greek keeps it.

The adjective is formed from the word for 'age', and in Jewish usage 'eternal life' is the life of the age to come: a kind of life as well as an unending one. Verse 3 gives this Gospel's own definition of it as knowing God and the one he sent. 'Eternal' is the standard rendering; a minority of translators prefer 'life of the age to come'.

In biblical idiom a person's name stands for who that person is: character, identity and authority. To reveal God's name is to make God himself known, not merely to disclose a title. Some interpreters also hear an allusion to the divine name of Exodus 3, but that is debated.

Older translations have 'I pray for them'. The verb is the everyday word for asking or making a request, and this Gospel does not use the usual Greek verb for praying at all. Many modern translations likewise render it 'ask'.

The Greek preposition can mean 'in' (kept within the sphere of what God's name stands for) or 'by' (protected by the power of that name). Translations divide between the two, and the same question arises in verse 12.

notes.traditional: those whom thou hast given me
notes.note: The earliest and best manuscripts read 'your name, which you have given me', so that what is given is the name. Later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, read 'those whom you have given me', making the disciples what is given. Modern editions and most modern translations follow the earlier reading here and in verse 12.

'Son of' is a Semitic idiom for someone who belongs to or is destined for a thing. In Greek the noun shares its root with the verb just translated 'was lost', so the phrase says in effect that the only one lost was the one who belonged to loss. Judas is meant, and the scripture in view is usually taken to be Psalm 41:9, quoted at John 13:18.

The Greek form can be masculine ('the evil one', the devil) or neuter ('evil' in general). Most modern translations and commentators choose the personal sense, in line with this Gospel's references to 'the ruler of this world' and with 1 John 5:18–19. The King James Version has 'the evil'.

The traditional 'sanctify' now suggests gradual moral improvement. In the Greek Old Testament this verb is used for setting people and offerings apart for God's service, such as priests, prophets and sacrifices. That is the sense in verse 19, where Jesus consecrates himself. The verb is related to 'holy' in the address 'Holy Father' in verse 11; several modern translations also use 'consecrate' here.

Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, read 'that they also may be one in us'. Important early manuscripts lack the word 'one' here, and most modern editions regard it as a copyist's addition echoing the opening of the verse.

candidates.reason: Translators vary between 'sanctify', 'consecrate' and 'make holy' across John, Paul and Hebrews; the link to ἅγιος and the register's handling of 'holy ones' call for one decision.
Central in John and frequent elsewhere; 'glorify', 'honour' and 'praise' are all in use, and variation would obscure John's glory theme.
Used both for keeping a word or command and for keeping people safe; 'keep', 'obey', 'protect' and 'guard' compete, and this chapter plays on both senses.
Rendered 'pray' in older versions and 'ask' in modern ones; the distinction from αἰτέω and προσεύχομαι should be handled consistently.
Rendered variously 'finish', 'complete', 'perfect' and 'accomplish' in John, Hebrews and 1 John; the traditional 'perfect' can mislead and needs one policy.
